newsitem.title: POLAND: ONE MILLION GATHER AT CATHOLIC CONGRESS IN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: ONE MILLION GATHER AT CATHOLIC CONGRESS IN POLAND.

text.p: The first of an expected one million pilgrims began gathering in the west Poland city of Wroclaw on Sunday for a major world gathering of Catholics which will culminate in a visit by Pope John Paul on May 31.

At an opening ceremony Wroclaw Archbishop Henryk Gulbinowicz welcomed guests of various faiths, Catholic clergy and lay people from 86 countries who will attend lectures, seminars and religious services during the week-long event.

The 46th International Eucharistic Congress is the first to be held in Eastern Europe which overthrew communism eight years ago and it will consider how to build a better world based on love of God and man, Polish public television reported.
"May the people of the waning 20th century look at this congress and say, as pagans did in the early centuries of Christianity: 'Look how they love one another'," Gulbinowicz said.

Speaking in the city's renovated Hitler-era People's Hall, the cardinal said Wroclaw, not far from the German and Czech borders, could become an international gathering place which he likened to "the Strasbourg of Central Europe."
Wroclaw, a city of 645,000, was among formerly German-ruled areas ceded to Poland after the World War Two.
The Polish-born Pontiff will spend two days of his fifth and longest-ever 11-day pilgrimage to his homeland at the congress.

The congress is taking place against the backdrop of a tug-of-war between Poland's secular-minded leftists and liberals, who regard the Church's influence as excessive, and right-leaning pro-Catholic groups.
Its battlefields include Sunday's nationwide referendum to decide the fate of a constitutional draft, which many Catholics oppose, and September's parliamentary elections.

The autumn poll is expected to be largely a contest between the co-ruling ex-communists and an alliance of right-wing parties led by the Solidarity trade-union movement which have been been neck in neck in opinion surveys for months.
The first Eucharistic Congress, held in France in the 1870s, was called to promote devotion to the Blessed Sacrament and to counteract the inroads of secularisation.
